analysis_notes.notes: Torah LM2 #21 contains exactly one dataset edge with reference 1021, and it is classified as 'eitza' (cause-effect), not 'bechina'. There are zero bechina edges for this Torah. The single eitza edge is: 'ללמד פוסקים קדם החדוש שמחדש ואחר כך' → 'נעשין בחינת אנשי חיל מלפניהם ומלאחריהם' — studying Poskim before and after the chiddush PRODUCES the effect of soldiers standing guard. The source text uses the phrase 'נַעֲשִׂין בְּחִינַת אַנְשֵׁי־חַיִל', but this is adjectival (the Poskim become/function AS soldiers), not a structural equation between two co-equal concepts sharing the same nature. The underlying relationship is causal: studying Poskim causes/produces the protective guard of anshei chayil. This is correctly classified as eitza. The Torah text is exceptionally brief (two sentences) and teaches one practical principle — the need to learn Poskim before and after innovating Torah — without establishing bechina (parallel-nature) equations between concepts. No bechina-language statements of the form 'X הוא בְּחִינַת Y' appear in the source. Therefore, no packages can be formed from bechina-connected nodes, no gap additions are identified, and no orphaned dataset nodes exist.
